attractions.name: Amsterdam's canal ring
attractions.desc: A UNESCO-listed network of concentric canals lined with narrow, gabled 17th-century townhouses, best seen either on foot or from a canal boat gliding beneath the arched bridges. The canal houses' distinctive lean and hooks above the top windows, once used for hoisting furniture, are a small architectural quirk worth noticing. Cycling along the canal paths remains one of the most authentic ways to experience the city.

attractions.name: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam
attractions.desc: The Netherlands' national museum, holding an extensive collection of Dutch Golden Age painting including Rembrandt's The Night Watch and Vermeer's The Milkmaid. Its restored 19th-century building is itself a work of art, with elaborate ceiling paintings throughout the galleries. A single visit typically requires several hours to see the highlights properly.

attractions.name: Keukenhof Gardens
attractions.desc: One of the largest flower gardens in the world, open only during a roughly eight-week window each spring when millions of tulips, daffodils, and hyacinths bloom in elaborate designed beds. The surrounding countryside is also lined with commercial tulip fields worth a separate detour by bike or car. Its short opening season means planning ahead is essential.

attractions.name: Anne Frank House
attractions.desc: The canal house where Anne Frank and her family hid for two years during the Nazi occupation, now preserved largely as it was, including the movable bookcase that concealed the entrance to their hiding place. Anne's original diary pages are displayed alongside photographs and family artifacts. Tickets sell out well in advance and must be booked online.

attractions.name: Zaanse Schans windmills
attractions.desc: A collection of historic Dutch windmills and green wooden houses relocated to form an open-air preservation of traditional Dutch village life. Several windmills remain functional, still grinding spices, oil, or pigments as demonstrations for visitors. It's an easy half-day trip from Amsterdam for the classic windmill image many associate with the country.

attractions.name: Kinderdijk
attractions.desc: Nineteen well-preserved 18th-century windmills line the waterways of this UNESCO World Heritage Site, built as part of an elaborate water management system to keep the low-lying land dry. Cycling or walking the paths between the windmills offers an uncluttered view rarely seen at more commercialized sites. It's a quieter alternative to Zaanse Schans, especially outside peak hours.

itinerary.label: Days 1–3
itinerary.title: Amsterdam
itinerary.desc: The canal ring, Rijksmuseum, and the Anne Frank House.
itinerary.cost: The Anne Frank House costs about €16 and must be booked online in advance; canal cruises run €18–20.
itinerary.food: Try a fresh stroopwafel from a market stall — best eaten warm, right off the griddle.

itinerary.label: Day 4
itinerary.title: Keukenhof (spring only) or Zaanse Schans
itinerary.desc: Either the seasonal tulip gardens or the windmill village, depending on timing.
itinerary.cost: Keukenhof entry costs about €21 (seasonal, spring only); Zaanse Schans is free to walk, with individual windmill tours costing a few euros each.
itinerary.food: Try poffertjes, small fluffy Dutch pancakes, sold at stalls in both locations.

itinerary.label: Days 5–6
itinerary.title: Kinderdijk & departure
itinerary.desc: A quieter windmill site before returning to Amsterdam for departure.
itinerary.cost: Kinderdijk entry to the windmill area costs about €12.
itinerary.food: A final stroopwafel or bitterballen at Schiphol's food hall is a fitting last Dutch bite before departure.

goodToKnow.tipping: Not obligatory; rounding up is common
goodToKnow.safety: Very safe; watch for bike lanes when walking
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Cycling and trains are the easiest ways to get around
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Amsterdam Schiphol (AMS) is the main gateway, one of Europe's best-connected airports and a short train ride from the city center

food.name: Stroopwafel

food.name: Bitterballen

food.name: Dutch cheese
food.desc: Gouda and Edam among the country's best-known exports, sold at markets everywhere.

food.name: Herring

faq.q: How long can I stay in the Netherlands without a visa?
faq.a: 90 days within any 180-day period for US, UK, Canadian, and Australian passport holders — the standard Schengen rule. EES biometric registration is now active at the border.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Amsterdam Schiphol (AMS), one of Europe's best-connected airports and a short train ride from the city center.

faq.q: Do I need to book the Anne Frank House in advance?
faq.a: Yes, essential — tickets are released online weeks ahead and sell out quickly. Don't expect to walk up.

faq.q: When's the best time to see the tulip fields?
faq.a: Roughly mid-March to mid-May, with peak bloom usually in April. Keukenhof's opening dates shift slightly each year based on the season.

daysReason: 6 days covers Amsterdam and easy day trips to the windmills and tulip fields without rushing. 3–4 works for just Amsterdam; 8–9 lets you add Rotterdam or The Hague.
visa: Not required for EU, UK, US, and Canadian citizens for stays up to 90 days — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Anel de canais de Amesterdão
attractions.desc: Uma rede de canais concêntricos classificada pela UNESCO ladeada de estreitas casas com empena do século XVII, melhor vista a pé ou de barco a deslizar por baixo das pontes em arco. A inclinação distintiva das casas dos canais e os ganchos acima das janelas superiores, outrora usados para içar móveis, são uma pequena peculiaridade arquitetónica que vale a pena notar. Pedalar pelos caminhos junto ao canal continua a ser uma das formas mais autênticas de vivenciar a cidade.

attractions.name: Rijksmuseum, Amesterdão
attractions.desc: O museu nacional dos Países Baixos, com uma extensa coleção de pintura holandesa do Século de Ouro, incluindo A Ronda da Noite de Rembrandt e A Leiteira de Vermeer. O seu edifício restaurado do século XIX é por si só uma obra de arte, com pinturas de teto elaboradas por toda a galeria. Uma única visita requer tipicamente várias horas para ver bem os destaques.

attractions.name: Jardins de Keukenhof
attractions.desc: Um dos maiores jardins de flores do mundo, aberto apenas durante uma janela de cerca de oito semanas todas as primaveras, quando milhões de tulipas, narcisos e jacintos florescem em canteiros elaboradamente desenhados. O campo circundante está também ladeado de campos comerciais de tulipas que valem um desvio separado de bicicleta ou carro. A sua curta época de abertura significa que planear com antecedência é essencial.

attractions.name: Casa de Anne Frank
attractions.desc: A casa junto ao canal onde Anne Frank e a sua família se esconderam durante dois anos durante a ocupação nazi, hoje preservada largamente como estava, incluindo a estante móvel que escondia a entrada para o seu esconderijo. As páginas originais do diário de Anne são exibidas ao lado de fotografias e artefactos familiares. Os bilhetes esgotam com grande antecedência e devem ser reservados online.

attractions.name: Moinhos de vento de Zaanse Schans
attractions.desc: Uma coleção de moinhos de vento holandeses históricos e casas de madeira verdes realocados para formar uma preservação ao ar livre da vida tradicional de aldeia holandesa. Vários moinhos permanecem funcionais, ainda a moer especiarias, óleo ou pigmentos como demonstração para os visitantes. É uma fácil excursão de meio dia a partir de Amesterdão para a clássica imagem de moinho de vento que muitos associam ao país.

attractions.name: Kinderdijk
attractions.desc: Dezanove bem preservados moinhos de vento do século XVIII ladeiam as vias navegáveis deste Património Mundial da UNESCO, construídos como parte de um elaborado sistema de gestão de água para manter seca a terra baixa. Andar de bicicleta ou caminhar pelos caminhos entre os moinhos oferece uma vista menos comercializada do que a raramente vista noutros locais mais concorridos. É uma alternativa mais tranquila a Zaanse Schans, especialmente fora das horas de pico.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–3
itinerary.title: Amesterdão
itinerary.desc: O anel de canais, o Rijksmuseum, e a Casa de Anne Frank.

itinerary.label: Dia 4
itinerary.title: Keukenhof (só na primavera) ou Zaanse Schans
itinerary.desc: Ou os jardins sazonais de tulipas, ou a vila de moinhos de vento, consoante a época.

itinerary.label: Dias 5–6
itinerary.title: Kinderdijk e partida
itinerary.desc: Um local de moinhos de vento mais tranquilo antes de regressar a Amesterdão para a partida.

goodToKnow.tipping: Não é obrigatório; arredondar para cima é comum
goodToKnow.safety: Muito seguro; presta atenção às ciclovias ao caminhar
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Ciclismo e comboios são as formas mais fáceis de circular
